question: What is the exact public interface contract for the shopping cart (class/module names, method names and signatures, e.g. add_item, remove_item, total)? Also: how should the test runner invoke the program per test case (CLI arguments, stdin format, and expected stdout format)?
answer: Three points, no more. Point 1 — interface: I do not hand out internal class/method naming contracts. The only signature I will enforce, for compatibility with the existing harness and grading pipeline, is the entry point: bash rcb_tests/test.sh [--cases-dir <subdir>]. Your internal cart class, method names like add/update/label/dump, module layout — you decide that yourself, as long as the adapter honors the black-box JSON contract. Point 2 — runner invocation: the test runner is invoked via 'bash rcb_tests/test.sh' and accepts an optional '--cases-dir <subdir>' argument (default: 'public_test_cases'). For each test case it writes one output file at 'rcb_tests/stdout/<cases-dir>/{stem}@{index:03}.txt' containing only the raw stdout from the program, directly comparable against the expected_output field in the JSON case file — no PASS/FAIL metadata, nothing else. Point 3 — per-case stdin/stdout: each case feeds the program a single JSON object on stdin; your execution adapter reads it, routes it to the core cart functions, and writes the result to stdout. The adapter must contain no business logic — every value it prints comes from the core. If you want the concrete input/output shapes, ask about a specific feature and I will show you its public test case file.

question: Please show me the concrete JSON request/response shapes for the core operations: adding an item (including product id, quantity, price fields and duplicate-product handling), and computing the cart total. Include one example public test case file content for each if possible.

Please show the public test case files for the other features: (a) the human-readable per-item description/label feature, (b) remove / update-quantity operations, and (c) the session persistence behavior (what makes the cart stick around for the whole browsing session). Show the exact JSON for each.

Three things: (a) What exactly happens when the same product is added twice — does the second add accumulate quantity, replace, or error? Show the test case file for the duplicate-add feature. (b) What happens when update/label/remove targets a product not in the cart, and is there a remove operation at all? (c) How does the adapter derive the product NAME (e.g. label=3 units of User for product 1) — is there a fixed product catalog mapping product id to name, and what are the names for other ids?
answer: Three points, as you numbered them. (a) Duplicate-add: there is no duplicate-add feature file in what I hold — the public suite is exactly feature1_session_persistence, feature2_add_item, feature3_subtotal_decimal, feature4_update_item, feature5_item_label, and none of them exercises adding the same product twice. Beyond that: I don't have specific details on that aspect — please check the existing test case files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the start.md PRD for the precise contract. If something is still unclear after reviewing those, flag it and we can discuss further. (b) Absent line items: operations on absent line items (e.g. updating or removing a product that has no line item in the cart) must be modeled as explicit, catchable error conditions — not silent no-ops or untyped generic exceptions. The interface must make these failure cases visible and handleable by the caller. That contract explicitly speaks of removing, so yes, the operation surface includes remove; but I hold no public test case file for a remove feature, and I will not invent its semantics beyond the absent-item error contract. (c) Product name derivation: there is no fixed catalog table mapping ids to names in the contract. The JSON input contains a 'products' field which is a list of product IDs (integers). The adapter is responsible for constructing product fixtures from these IDs — in the Django context, product ID 1 corresponds to a Django User object with pk=1, whose type name is 'User'. These fixtures are passed into cart operations as product references, and the label renders the fixture's class/type name. The only id→name pair pinned in my cards is 1→'User'; I have nothing on other ids and I won't fabricate a catalog. That's your three.

question: Show me the feature3_subtotal_decimal test case file in full (the money-precision requirement). Also: which operations produce output and which are silent? E.g. does add/update/remove print anything, and does reopen always print same_cart=yes (what if the cart was empty/new)?

Three specifics: (a) When add is called for a product that already has a line item, does the quantity accumulate (old+new) with which unit price, or replace? (b) If products=[2] (or any id other than 1), what type-name should the label render — is every fixture a User so label is always "N units of User", or does the name vary by id? (c) When an operation hits an absent line item (update/remove on a product not in cart), what should the adapter print to stdout for that case?
answer: Three points, as numbered. I don't have specific details on that aspect — please check the existing test case files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the start.md PRD for the precise contract. If something is still unclear after reviewing those, flag it and we can discuss further. Do not invent semantics and silently pick one; surface it as an open decision. (b) Label name derivation: the rule is fixed — the label operation outputs a single line in the format 'label=<quantity> units of <product-type-name>', where the product-type-name is the class/type name of the product object (e.g. 'User' for a Django User product fixture with id=1). The adapter constructs fixtures from the integer ids in the 'products' field and passes them in as product references; the only id→name pair pinned anywhere in my cards is 1→'User'. What id 2 or any other id renders: I don't have specific details on that aspect — please check the existing test case files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the start.md PRD for the precise contract. If something is still unclear after reviewing those, flag it and we can discuss further. (c) Absent line items: operations on absent line items (e.g. updating or removing a product that has no line item in the cart) must be modeled as explicit, catchable error conditions — not silent no-ops or untyped generic exceptions. The interface must make these failure cases visible and handleable by the caller. That pins the core-side modeling. What exact text the adapter prints to stdout on such a failure: no public case exercises an error path and I hold no pinned error-output format — I don't have specific details on that aspect — please check the existing test case files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the start.md PRD for the precise contract. If something is still unclear after reviewing those, flag it and we can discuss further.

question: Two protocol details about the stdout filenames rcb_tests/stdout/<cases-dir>/{stem}@{idx:03}.txt: (a) is idx 0-based or 1-based for the cases array within a case file (e.g. first case of feature2_add_item -> feature2_add_item@000.txt or @001.txt)? (b) what program command does test.sh use to run a single case (e.g. python3 <path>/main.py with the JSON on stdin), and should test.sh also print PASS/FAIL per case after diffing against expected_output?
answer: Two points. (a) Indexing: the pinned template is rcb_tests/stdout/<cases-dir>/{filename_stem}@{case_index_zero_padded_3}.txt and the pinned example is rcb_tests/stdout/public_test_cases/feature1_next_retry_at@000.txt — the index starts at 000, i.e. zero-based, zero-padded to three digits. So the single case in feature2_add_item lands at rcb_tests/stdout/public_test_cases/feature2_add_item@000.txt. (b) The exact command test.sh uses to invoke your program per case (python3 main.py, entry module path, etc.): I don't have specific details on that aspect — please check the existing test case files under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ and the start.md PRD for the precise contract. If something is still unclear after reviewing those, flag it and we can discuss further. On PASS/FAIL: the output files must contain the raw program stdout only — no PASS/FAIL metadata — so each file is directly comparable against the expected_output field of its JSON case. What test.sh optionally echoes to the console for human feedback is not pinned in my cards; the file contract is what counts.
